People from a template

A test for Moon Faire, November 13. The Jester's finished model is the template. A Claude model reads one line about a person and writes a small file: colours, skin, a repainted face, hair, a hat, clothes. The Jester's skeleton and all her moves are reused, so every person can already stand, turn and walk. The lamp-seller was made by hand; the rest were made through your API key.

What it cost

Three tests, twenty-four people, all through your key, for $12.69 in all (that includes about 35 cents for writing the skin prompts). The first test gave four one-line descriptions to three models at their default settings, written for people seen small. After you ruled that the only people in the game are ones the party talks to, the second test gave the same four lines to Opus 5.5 at high and at extra-high effort, written for a person seen up close, with up to three fixes. The third gave them to Fable 5.2 the same way.

Made byEach personTime

    Prices are the list prices on Anthropic's pricing page on November 13, 2026, applied to the token counts each reply reported.

    What this says
    • Opus 5.5 at high effort is the setting to use: about 38 cents and two minutes a person. Extra-high costs about $1.33 and seven minutes for little more. Fable 5.2 through the key costs about $1.08 and comes out about level with Opus at high.
    • The lamp-seller is better than all of them for two reasons that are not the model: she was made by hand with several looks and adjustments, and an old woman in a long skirt, apron and kerchief suits the template.
    • What decides whether a person is good enough is mostly the design, not the price. A woman in long clothes (the lamp-seller, the fortune-teller) suits the template and holds up. A man does not yet, because every person has the Jester's body and the shape of her face.
    • Each person is about 12 thousand triangles and 15 draws. The Jester took 106 thousand when she walked the fair square on your laptop. No Claude session can measure speed on your laptop.

    Make one yourself

    This part works when the page is opened as a file on your computer (the copy sent in the chat). It talks to Anthropic directly from your browser with your key, so it uses API credit and no Claude subscription. The key stays in this page's memory and is gone when you close it.

    The lamp-seller, then the second and third tests

    The four descriptions are stand-ins written for this test, not Moon Faire lore. Each picture shows front, three-quarter, side, back, walking, and the face twice. The twelve people of the first test are in the menu under the 3D view.
